title: Public protection and falling objects
moduleTitle: Group (Exterior, height & access): Safety and hazards
audience: Trainee or new worker on the pressure cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify safety and authorisation decisions associated with public protection and falling objects.
Explain the applicable risk hierarchy and specialist responsibilities for public protection and falling objects.
Produce a defensible stop-work, competent-person referral or restricted handover using mock evidence.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the pressure cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level pressure work and elevated or roof-level applications. High-pressure water, hoses and lances, electrical supply, exhaust gases and falls are all hazards on this track. Work above ground level is restricted to workers who are authorised by the employer and who hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Purpose and assessable outcome
instruction.body: The learner must recognise public exclusion and interface control in the context of public protection and falling objects, identify evidence gaps, and prepare a safe decision record. Trainer distinguishes observation, inference and approval.

instruction.heading: Authorised scope and information needed
instruction.body: Review fictional work orders, site controller details, current method approval and the location-specific risk assessment. Map people moving underneath and beside a work area; never assume tape or a sign alone proves adequate protection. Document missing information as an open decision, not implicit permission.

instruction.heading: Hazard and safer-option analysis
instruction.body: Analyse the lesson case: A shopping entrance remains open beneath a proposed upper-storey cleaning location. Start with avoiding elevated work and select no method until competency, protection of third parties and site constraints are established. Escalate uncertainties before dispatch.

instruction.heading: Role boundaries and stop-work decision
instruction.body: Recommended decision: Withhold commencement until the responsible controller has approved effective public protection and access separation. General cleaning training cannot sign off rope descent, platform operation, anchor certification, electrical clearance or emergency rescue capability.

instruction.heading: Evidence, communication and quality
instruction.body: Use dated simulated records to show the exact observation, source document, person notified, time, restriction and requested response. Refer to course research ha94-uk-window; do not claim a jurisdiction is approved.

instruction.heading: Trainer-led tabletop practice
instruction.body: Map hypothetical pedestrian flows and mark where the submitted controls fail to protect people below. Use photographs, drawn plans, fictitious work orders and inert desk materials only. Trainer checks accuracy and intervenes if the learner proposes unauthorised real-world activities.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Review the work order, the site controller's details, the current method approval and the location-specific risk assessment.
Map the people moving underneath and beside the work area.
Check the submitted controls against those people, and do not accept tape or a sign alone as proof of protection.
Start by avoiding elevated work, and select no method until competency, protection of third parties and site constraints are established.
Record any missing information as an open decision, not as implicit permission.
Escalate any uncertainty to the responsible controller before dispatch.
Withhold commencement until the responsible controller has approved effective public protection and access separation.
Record the observation, the source document, the person notified, the time, the restriction and the response requested.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed below that (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: People moving below and beside the work area are mapped before any decision is made.
Tape or a sign alone is never accepted as proof of protection.
Work does not start until the responsible controller approves public protection and access separation.
Submitted controls that fail to protect people below are marked and escalated.
summary: Public exclusion and separation are checked by mapping people moving under and beside a work area.
Tape or a sign alone is not accepted as adequate protection against falling objects.
Commencement is withheld until the responsible controller has approved effective public protection and access separation.

knowledgeChecks.question: For public protection and falling objects, what evidence must be established before allocating work, and which facts are still unverified?
options: A taped line or sign alone, which shows that people below are protected, and a verbal assurance from the crew leader that the people below are clear and the work can begin
That the work can start, since the tape is in place, and the approvals can follow, and the pedestrians have been told to keep clear of the walkway for the day
The current method approval, the location risk assessment and the site controller's approval of public separation, with pedestrian protection unverified until then
That general cleaning training covers rope descent and platform operation, and the rope access training is current for the crew and the supervisor

knowledgeChecks.question: Does a taped line or a sign alone prove that people below are adequately protected?
options: Yes, if the tape is red
